provenance.instrument: Zoning Ordinance of the City of Butler (Chapter 260 Zoning, adopted 2-19-1987 as Part 13 of the 1987 Codified Ordinances, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 BU1538, City of Butler, Butler County. Chapter 260 was adopted 2-19-1987 and amended many times, most recently by Ord. No. 1825 (9-25-2024, mobile homes). New Laws lists Ord. No. 1842, 1843 and 1844 (2026), none of them on zoning. Each district article lists its uses and lot and yard figures in the text, and those were read. The Bulk and Dimensional table (Attachment 1, 2014) and the Use Table were read on 2026-11-26: the lot areas, front, rear and accessory yards, heights and coverage match the text, side yards are given there as shares of lot width (10% one side, 30% total), and the Use Table permits a conversion of a single-family house to two units in R-2 and R-3 and to multifamily in R-3 (P*), two-family dwellings in R-2, R-3 and R-O, and no accessory dwelling use
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360: 'Includes legislation through 05-28-2026.' New Laws (3), none on zoning
checks: The zoning chapter has no accessory dwelling unit, in-law suite or similar use
Each district lists its uses 'for the following uses only' (260-13, 260-20, 260-29, 260-38, 260-46, 260-56)

R-1: 'No more than one dwelling unit shall be permitted on any lot or property in the R-1 District except under the planned residential development requirements' (260-16A). R-2: no more than two dwelling units on any lot (260-24A)

'No accessory building shall be used for dwelling purposes, unless the main building on the lot is also being used for dwelling purposes and all other requirements of this chapter are met' (260-10L). Where a district allows more than one unit, units in an accessory building count toward the district's maximum (260-10N)

Conversion of a single-family house that existed before the chapter (2-19-1987) to two units is a permitted use in R-2 and R-3, with no Zoning Hearing Board review unless a variance is needed: 450 sq ft of living space per unit and a 3,000 sq ft lot with no exterior addition (260-20C, 260-29D, 260-132D(4)(a))
An accessory building attached to the main building by a common wall or roof is part of the main building (260-7 'Accessory')
Sheds stand only in a side or rear yard, at most one per 3,000 sq ft of lot and two per lot, and may stand within the setbacks (260-14B, 260-16D(2))
A mobile home may be placed only as the principal structure on a lot (260-89)
Off-street parking: two spaces per unit for a single-family or two-family dwelling, one per conversion apartment (260-118A)
In the Ritts Historical and Architectural District, parcels zoned R-2, R-3 or C-2 were rezoned R-1, and the R-1 rules apply to every parcel there (260-145, 260-146)
A dwelling unit has all its rooms joined, with 'access through an interior door' to all other parts of the unit (260-7 'Dwelling unit')
A shed is at most 144 sq ft and 12.5 ft tall, and a shed 'may not be used as a dwelling' (260-7 'Shed')

Townhouses are a conditional use in R-1, R-2, R-3, R-O and C-1: a lot of at least 6,000 sq ft and at most one unit per 3,000 sq ft (260-15H, 260-22H, 260-31M, 260-40D, 260-48H). R-3 also lists row dwellings by conditional use (260-31F)
A traditional neighborhood development is a conditional use in R-1, R-2 and R-3 on at least 5 acres (260-15A, 260-97, 260-98D). It is the planned residential development that 260-16A refers to
provenance.notes: Zoning office: City of Butler, Zoning and Code Management Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360, one page at a time, on 2026-11-15, in print view. Searched the code (scope all) for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, accessory suite, ECHO, elder cottage, granny, guest house, carriage house, tenant house, living quarters, second dwelling, conversion, two-family, caretaker, farm dwelling, relative and relative quarters. Hits were the two-family and conversion apartment definitions, the conversion listings in R-2 and R-3, the caretaker and watchman quarters in C-1, C-2 and M-1, 260-125 and the rental occupancy chapter. Read: Articles I, III, V to XIII, XV, XVI, XVIII to XX and XXIII. Read in part: Article II definitions (A to 'Lot width' in full, the rest by search and term list). Not read: Article IV (district list), XIV (floodplain), XVII (signs), XXI (amendments), XXII (administration), XXIV (Rotary Arts and Cultural District) and the PDF attachments. Height is measured from the average finished grade to the highest point of a flat roof or the average height of the highest gable of a pitched roof. Coverage counts buildings only. No unlisted-use rule for houses: the R-2 and R-3 'similar' conditional uses reach only neighborhood commercial activities, and the C-1, C-2, M-1 and M-2 ones only commercial or industrial uses. Second reading 2026-11-26 (G0): eCode360 now 'legislation through 05-28-2026'. Bulk and Dimensional table and Use Table read by cell position and match the file (see status_detail). The zoning map is not needed for the rule. Left as disputes the code does not settle: the conversion cutoff date (read as the chapter's adoption, 2-19-1987, which may re-enact an older date), and whether a dwelling unit in an accessory building is allowed at all (260-10N counts such units, but no use list names one; kept as an alternative where two or more units are allowed).

term.note: Searched the code for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, accessory suite, ECHO, elder cottage, granny, guest house, carriage house, tenant house, living quarters, second dwelling, conversion, two-family, caretaker, farm dwelling and relative, and read every district's use list. No ADU use

status.note: No district lists a second dwelling unit on a single-family lot. Each district permits its listed uses only. R-2, R-3 and R-O permit two-family dwellings, and R-2 and R-3 permit the conversion of an older house to two units (see the alternatives)

path.note: A second unit on a single-family lot is not a listed use. The code bars a use variance for a use the district does not permit (260-132C(4)), so the routes left are the listed two-unit uses or a zoning amendment

fallback_path.note: Dimensional relief from the Zoning Hearing Board on the five findings of 260-132C(1). Not a use variance

use_variance_barred.quote: Under no circumstances shall the Board grant a variance to allow a use not permissible under the terms of this chapter in the district involved or any use expressly or by implication prohibited by the terms of this chapter in the district

value.name: Conversion of an existing single-family house to two dwelling units (R-2, R-3)
value.conditions: 'Conversion of a single-family residence existing prior to the adoption of this chapter to two dwelling units' is a permitted use in R-2 (260-20C), and to two or more units in R-3 (260-29D). It 'does not require review by the Zoning Hearing Board unless a variance is requested' (260-132D(4)(a)). At least 450 sq ft of living space per unit, the city Housing Code, safe entry and exit, one off-street space per conversion apartment (260-118A). With no exterior addition the building is presumed to meet the yard, height and coverage rules. An addition must meet every district rule. Lot: 3,000 sq ft for a two-family conversion with no exterior addition in R-2 and R-3, plus 1,500 sq ft for each unit over two in R-3

requires.condition: The house existed before the zoning chapter was adopted (2-19-1987)
At least 450 sq ft of living space for each dwelling unit

value.note: The chapter history gives 2-19-1987 as its adoption, so a house built before then is read as qualifying. That chapter may re-enact an older ordinance, so the cutoff date is a reading. 260-132D(4) sits under the heading 'The following special exceptions are subject to special conditions', but (4)(a) says no Zoning Hearing Board review is needed, so it is read as by right. In the Ritts Historical and Architectural District the R-1 rules apply, and R-1 allows one dwelling unit per lot (260-146, 260-16A)

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-2, R-3, R-O)
value.conditions: A two-family dwelling is 'A detached building designed exclusively for occupancy by two families living independently of each other and containing two dwelling units' (260-7). Permitted in R-2 (260-20B), R-3 (260-29B) and R-O (260-38B). Lot 7,000 sq ft in R-2 (260-24B(2)), 4,000 sq ft in R-3 (260-33A(2)) and R-O (260-42A(2)). Two off-street spaces per unit (260-118A)
value.note: The two units share one detached building

value.name: Dwelling unit in an accessory building where the district allows two or more units
value.conditions: 'Where more than one dwelling unit is permitted, all the dwelling units shall be in the same building except in the case of a planned residential development or in the case of a dwelling unit or units existing or created in an accessory building on the lot, in which case the number of dwelling units in both the principal building and accessory building combined shall not exceed the maximum number permitted for the zone district' (260-10N). An accessory building may be used for dwelling purposes only if the main building is also used as a dwelling and all other requirements are met (260-10L). R-2 allows at most two units per lot (260-24A). The lot may not be divided unless each new lot meets the district minimums
value.note: The lot figure shown is the two-family figure, which is a reading

disputed_path.note: No district use list names a house with a unit in an accessory building. A two-family dwelling is one detached building with two units, and a dwelling group (two or more buildings each with one or more units) is listed in no district. 260-10N may only count such units against the cap where they already exist. The code bars a use variance for a use the district does not permit (260-132C(4))

value.name: Dwelling units on the upper floors of a commercial building (C-1)
value.conditions: 'Dwelling units on the upper floor or floors of a building, the first or ground level floor of which, facing the street to which the property has its principal access, is used for or is available and designed for a C-1 permitted or approved conditional use, provided that the number of dwelling units does not exceed the total property area in square feet divided by 1,500, fractions excluded' (260-48D). City Council decides after a Planning Commission recommendation and a public hearing (260-106)
value.note: The host is a commercial building, not a house. C-1 lists no house

value.name: Townhouses (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-O, C-1)
value.conditions: Townhouses are a conditional use 'provided that the following conditions are met in addition to those that normally apply in the zone district': a lot of at least 6,000 sq ft on a street with a paved width of at least 22 ft, and 'not more than one dwelling unit per 3,000 square feet of lot area'. Units may be sold only if each unit has its own lot on the principal street, at least 20 ft wide (260-15H, 260-22H, 260-31M, 260-40D, 260-48H). City Council decides after a Planning Commission recommendation and a public hearing (260-106)
value.note: Whether a house with one added unit can count as a townhouse building is not said. In R-1 the one-unit limit of 260-16A also stands. R-3 lists row dwellings by conditional use too (260-31F)

value.name: Traditional neighborhood development (R-1, R-2, R-3)
value.conditions: A traditional neighborhood development under Article XV is a conditional use in R-1, R-2 and R-3 (260-15A, 260-97). The tract must be at least 5 acres (260-98D)
value.note: A development of a whole tract, not a second unit on one house lot

value.name: Apartments and duplexes in C-2
value.conditions: 'Apartments, including new structures or dwelling units over commercial stores at street level' (260-56S), multiple-family dwellings and 'Duplexes, limited to locations that do not abut Main Street' (260-56OO, PP) are permitted. A residential use needs a lot of at least 6,000 sq ft, counting area used for commerce in the same structure (260-59B)
value.note: C-2 lists no single-family house. A house there is a nonconforming use, which may be altered and may add sheds, garages and similar accessory structures under the R-3 standards (260-57D, 260-125B)

value.name: Residential upper floors in a mixed-use building (M-1)
value.conditions: 'Mixed-use buildings, residential upper floors' are a conditional use in M-1 (260-68O). So are one-person-occupancy rooms on the second or higher floor of a building that existed when the subsection was adopted, with a separate entrance, 350 sq ft of lot area per room and one parking space for each two rooms (260-68B). City Council decides after a Planning Commission recommendation and a public hearing (260-106)
value.note: The host is a mixed-use building, not a house. M-1 lists no house. An existing one- or two-family dwelling there is a nonconforming use (260-67D)

historic_bypass.note: No historic ADU path found. The Ritts Historical and Architectural District applies the R-1 rules (260-146)

districts_read_no_listing.note: No district lists a second unit on a single-family lot. R-1 permits single-family detached dwellings, with townhouses and a traditional neighborhood development by conditional use. R-2 adds two-family dwellings and older-house conversions, R-3 multiple dwellings too, R-O single-family, two-family and multiple-family dwellings with offices. Townhouses are a conditional use in R-1, R-2, R-3, R-O and C-1, and R-3 row dwellings too. C-1 lists upper-floor units by conditional use and quarters for an owner, caretaker or watchman. M-1 lists residential upper floors in mixed-use buildings and one-person rooms on upper floors by conditional use, and quarters for an owner, caretaker or watchman. C-2 lists apartments, multiple-family dwellings and duplexes off Main Street. M-2 lists no dwelling

types_allowed.note: No ADU use. An accessory building may hold a dwelling unit only where the district allows more than one unit (see the alternatives)

spaces_required.note: No ADU use. Single-family and two-family dwellings: two spaces per dwelling unit. Conversion apartments: one space per dwelling unit

min_lot_sqft.note: Width 75 ft. 'No more than one dwelling unit shall be permitted on any lot or property in the R-1 District except under the planned residential development requirements' (260-16A). Any single lot of record in separate ownership may hold a single-family dwelling and customary accessory buildings even if it is under the area or width minimum. The Zoning and Code Management Officer may approve up to 20% less than the area or yard minimums (260-121A)

setback_side_ft.note: Interior lot: 7.5 ft on one side, 22.5 ft for both sides. Corner lot: 15 ft on the street side and 7.5 ft on the other

accessory_setback_rear_ft.note: Accessory building rear yard. Sheds may stand within the setbacks, keeping safe sight distances (260-16D(2))

principal_max_height_ft.note: One-family dwelling. Other main structures 45 ft. Measured from the average finished grade around the building to the highest point of a flat roof, the deck line of a mansard roof, or the average height of the highest gable of a pitched or hip roof (260-7 'Building height')

max_building_coverage.note: The area occupied by buildings. Sheds are not counted. Accessory structures with more than 144 sq ft of floor space are counted

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family dwelling building. Two-family dwelling building 7,000 sq ft, other uses 6,000 sq ft. Width 50 ft. 'No more than two dwelling units shall be permitted on any lot or parcel in the R-2 District' (260-24A). Any single lot of record in separate ownership may hold a single-family dwelling and customary accessory buildings even if it is under the area or width minimum. The Zoning and Code Management Officer may approve up to 20% less than the area or yard minimums (260-121A)

setback_side_ft.note: Interior lot: 5 ft on one side, 15 ft for both sides. Corner lot: 12.5 ft on the street side and 5 ft on the other

setback_sides_total_ft.note: 'both sides, 15 feet or one side, five feet'

accessory_setback_rear_ft.note: Accessory building rear yard. Sheds may stand within the setbacks, keeping safe sight distances (260-24D(3))

principal_max_height_ft.note: 'Except when authorized by Article XVI, no building shall exceed a height of three stories or 45 feet.' Measured from the average finished grade around the building to the highest point of a flat roof, the deck line of a mansard roof, or the average height of the highest gable of a pitched or hip roof (260-7 'Building height')

max_building_coverage.note: The area occupied by buildings. Sheds are not counted. Accessory structures with more than 144 sq ft of floor space are counted

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family dwelling. Two-family dwelling also 4,000 sq ft, multiple dwelling building 6,000 sq ft plus 500 sq ft for each unit over three (only efficiency and one-bedroom apartments: 350 sq ft more per unit, 260-33A(6)), other uses 5,000 sq ft. Width 40 ft for one- or two-family dwellings. The R-3 section sets no cap on units per lot in words. Any single lot of record in separate ownership may hold a single-family dwelling and customary accessory buildings even if it is under the area or width minimum. The Zoning and Code Management Officer may approve up to 20% less than the area or yard minimums (260-121A)

setback_side_ft.note: Interior lot: 4 ft on one side, 12 ft for both sides. Corner lot: 10 ft on the street side and 4 ft on the other

setback_sides_total_ft.note: 'both sides, 12 feet or one side, four feet'

accessory_setback_rear_ft.note: Accessory building rear yard. Sheds may stand within the setbacks, keeping safe sight distances (260-33C(3))

principal_max_height_ft.note: 'No building shall exceed a height of 80 feet.' Measured from the average finished grade around the building to the highest point of a flat roof, the deck line of a mansard roof, or the average height of the highest gable of a pitched or hip roof (260-7 'Building height')

max_building_coverage.note: The area occupied by buildings. Sheds are not counted. Accessory structures with more than 144 sq ft of floor space are counted

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family dwelling. Two-family dwelling also 4,000 sq ft, three-family 6,000 sq ft plus 500 sq ft for each further unit. Width 40 ft for one- or two-family dwellings. Any single lot of record in separate ownership may hold a single-family dwelling and customary accessory buildings even if it is under the area or width minimum. setback_front_ft.note: Where both neighbors' main buildings stand closer than 25 ft, the average of their front yards may be used

setback_side_ft.note: Interior lot: 4 ft on one side, 12 ft for both sides. Corner lot: 10 ft on the street side and 4 ft on the other

setback_sides_total_ft.note: 'both sides, 12 feet or one side, four feet'

accessory_setback_rear_ft.note: Accessory building rear yard. Sheds may stand within the setbacks, keeping safe sight distances (260-42C(3))
